shared_elements: frontal standing anthropomorphic figure filling the whole surface
elaborate headdress or head-covering at the top
relief carving on a rounded or slab-like block
museum display on a low plinth
justification: Both are tall stone monoliths carved with a single frontal figure organised the same way top-to-bottom — broad headdress/head element above, a chest disc or medallion at mid-height, and horizontal banded belt/limb ornaments below — which is a genuinely specific compositional correspondence. The rendering differs sharply, however: A is crisp, deeply undercut, densely detailed high relief with panelled glyph-like motifs, while B is coarse, shallow, heavily weathered and schematic with only a few incised lines, so they could not be the same hand.
